artifacts.summary: Round-4 summary extended with dispatch 38: the re-presentation family, the refutation of exists_tailStable_repr, the two asymmetric failure modes, and the Phase 17 design blocker.

decisions_made: exists_tailStable_repr is NOT stated in any form, because it is false. A weakened version (backward conjunct only, or under an extra closure hypothesis) was considered and rejected: the plan's own Phase 16 Scope Hypothesis forbids weakening a theorem to make it come out true, and a weakened lemma under that name would be read downstream as the harmlessness claim it is not.

The refutation is a FAMILY statement, not a single-certificate one. Proving only not cert.TailStable would have been consistent with the plan, which says an unstable certificate should be re-presented rather than rejected. Hence certRep a b c and not_tailStable (a b c).

The verdict went into a NEW module PlusSlicedCertificate/FixtureStable.lean rather than into Stable.lean, because Stable.lean imports Fixture.lean and the verdict needs both the fixture and Phi_fwd. Merging the two modules was the alternative and was rejected on the grounds the 16.1 record already gave for separating them.

The two failure modes are two separately named theorems, not one. Phi_back_L0_ne_cert is the pre-period showing through and IS repaired by the recipe (not_mem_L0_pR); Phi_fwd_R0_ne is repaired by nothing. Collapsing them would have hidden the asymmetry that makes this a design problem rather than a fixture artifact.

not_mem_L0_pR is stated only about the witness, not about Phi_back L0 = L0. It says the backward failure's witness leaves L0 once 1 <= b; it does NOT claim certRep a b c satisfies the backward conjunct, and its docstring says so.

Phase 17 is marked [BLOCKED] rather than started with a guessed repair, and Phase 16 is closed as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] rather than [PARTIAL], because nothing in Phase 16 changes whichever way the ruling goes and there is no residual Phase 16 work to hand off.
